scope_notes: Profile skill-pack, not the suggested agent-tool: README.md:140 says 'Ponytail is one prompt' (skills/ponytail/SKILL.md) and everything else loads it into ~35 hosts; agents do not call it to do work. Its runtime code (lifecycle hooks, the Claude Code band, the local board and the session importer, about 1,700 lines of JS/TS) is still scored under SEC, REL and PRV. red_line_decisions.suspected_red_lines: RL-3 (PRV-1 auto level 1) rejected: the probe's telemetry hits are benchmark fixture text (benchmarks/agentic/tasks.py:10,448,580; benchmarks/correctness.js:11); the only outbound call in shipped code is an opt-in, https-only webhook to a user-configured address (hooks/band/register.tsx:151-164, .claude-plugin/plugin.json:21-25).

gaps.title: Review benchmark figures have no published source
gaps.case: README.md:99 (review image text) states '100% of planted problems found, no skill 87%. 100% of problems outside the diff found, no skill 78%'; no file in benchmarks/results/ reports a review benchmark, and rg for 'planted' finds only tests/map.test.js:10.
gaps.impact: A headline-adjacent claim about /ponytail-review cannot be checked or reproduced.
gaps.fix: Publish the review benchmark (tasks, planted problems, runs, method) or remove the figures.

gaps.title: Board footer says nothing is estimated while imported costs are estimates
gaps.case: hooks/band/board.ts:555 ends the board with 'Cost is the API-priced cost Claude Code reports (/cost), not a bill. Nothing here is estimated.'; hooks/ponytail-band-import.js:16-56,152-160 computes imported sessions' cost from a hard-coded price table and keeps the larger of that estimate and Claude Code's own total ('the estimate runs 0-15% low').
gaps.impact: Users read estimated costs for imported sessions as reported ones.
gaps.fix: Mark imported or estimated rows on the board (the rows already carry level 'import') and reword the footer.

gaps.title: The band's test suite does not run in CI
gaps.case: tests/band.test.tsx (26 cases, including webhook https refusal and HTML escaping of a '<script>' task name) imports 'claude-code/testing' and is not matched by the npm test glob 'tests/*.test.js' (package.json:38); CI runs only npm test and the benchmark self-test (.github/workflows/test.yml:35-39).
gaps.impact: The band, ledger, board escaping and webhook token rules (about 1,400 lines under hooks/band/) can regress unnoticed.
gaps.fix: Run the band suite in CI, or port the pure-helper tests (metrics.ts, board.ts) to node --test.

gaps.title: Uninstall leaves the band's data behind, undocumented
gaps.case: scripts/uninstall.js:26-42 removes mode flags, config and the statusline copy but not ~/.config/ponytail/band/ (per-project CSV ledgers holding the first line of each task's first prompt, plus board.html) or ~/.claude/.ponytail-band; INSTALL.md:240 lists leftovers without them. The ledger is on by default (.claude-plugin/plugin.json:15-19) and 'band import' copies every past Claude Code session in (hooks/ponytail-band-import.js:216-266).
gaps.impact: Prompt excerpts and usage history persist after removal without notice (GDPR-style deletion expectations).
gaps.fix: Remove, or ask to remove, the band directory in uninstall.js and list it in INSTALL.md.

gaps.title: Review and audit read untrusted content without a data-not-instructions rule
gaps.case: /ponytail-review accepts 'a PR link' (skills/ponytail-review/SKILL.md:18-19) and /ponytail-audit reads whole repositories (skills/ponytail-audit/SKILL.md:18-26); neither skill tells the agent to treat that text as data. The codebase map, by contrast, filters to identifiers and is injection-tested (hooks/ponytail-map.js:21-22,67, tests/map.test.js:9-27).
gaps.impact: Instructions planted in a PR or repository can steer a review in hosts where the agent holds tools.
gaps.fix: Add the rule to both skills and an injected-PR case to the benchmark.

gaps.title: Headline statistic and raw runs are not shipped
gaps.case: benchmarks/results/2026-10-07-agentic.md:32-34 reports geometric means with 95% bootstrap intervals, but benchmarks/agentic/compare.py:78-91 computes median ratios and sign tests only, and run workspaces are gitignored (.gitignore:25-26). Recomputing from the published per-task medians reproduces the headline (lines -52.6% [-63, -41], cost -25.9% [-36, -16]).
gaps.impact: The numbers are consistent, but no one can recompute them from shipped code or rerun the statistics on raw data.
gaps.fix: Ship the aggregation script and a compressed results.json per release.

gaps.title: Unpinned CI tooling and a single-OS matrix
gaps.case: .github/workflows/test.yml:27 runs 'pip install pandas' without a version and :14 tests only on ubuntu-latest although Windows paths are supported (tests/hooks-windows.test.js simulates them); benchmarks/README.md:30 uses 'npx promptfoo@latest'; no update bot or vulnerability scan.
gaps.impact: CI results can change without a code change, and Windows or macOS regressions reach users first.
gaps.fix: Pin pandas, add windows-latest and macos-latest runners, pin promptfoo.

gaps.title: Third-party skill copy without its notice

The plugin installs the whole repository (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json:13).

opportunities.title: Extract the codebase map and reuse detector
opportunities.description: hooks/ponytail-map.js (identifier inventory under a character budget, injection-filtered and tested) and the band's definition, reuse and duplicate detectors (hooks/band/metrics.ts:35-90) are dependency-free and valuable without ponytail: RE4exa's rex gate (necessity check before building), t3code, orca and pandacode (agent GUIs) could show the same 'already exists' signal.

opportunities.title: The agentic benchmark as shared verification for skills
opportunities.description: Hidden checks with good and bad references, self-tested judges, mutation-based test-strength measurement and interleaved arms (benchmarks/agentic/) are generic. leanrea's 3-rep design cannot separate its arm from no skill (its review: wall ratio 0.87 [0.70, 1.05]); caveman and RE4exa evaluate skills too. One shared harness and task format would give all of them comparable numbers.

opportunities.title: Turn the ladder's checks into enforceable hooks
opportunities.description: The ladder is prose, but the band already detects new definitions that duplicate existing ones and callers left open after a removal (hooks/band/register.tsx:252-311). Exposing those as an optional post-edit warning or a pre-merge check would make 'already in this codebase?' and 'grep every caller' machine-checkable instead of model-dependent.

opportunities.title: Publish the task ledger as an open cost record
opportunities.description: The band's per-task row (session key, model, level, cost, turns, agent time, tokens, reuse, tests; hooks/band/metrics.ts:193-212,280) is a ready format for agent cost accounting. With caveman's offline token accounting, the run records of pi durable and absurd, and the agent GUIs (t3code, orca, pandacode) it could become one shared record instead of each tool inventing its own.

opportunities.title: Generate every rule copy from SKILL.md
opportunities.description: The rule text exists in 8 host copies, a JS fallback string (hooks/ponytail-instructions.js:43-75) and a Python port of the level filter (__init__.py:61-86); check-rule-copies.js itself names generation as the upgrade path. A build step would remove the hand-synced copies.

opportunities.title: Keep 10.9 MB of images out of plugin installs
opportunities.description: The Claude Code marketplace source is the whole repository (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json:13), so every plugin install carries 46 binaries totalling 10,929,610 bytes (localised banners and screenshots), while npm already excludes them (package.json:24-36).

questions.question: Is the README headline backed by the published benchmark?
questions.answer: Yes: -53% code and -26% cost with their intervals, and 30 of 38 cheaper tasks, reproduce from the published per-task table; the review figures (100%, 87%, 78%) have no published source.

questions.question: Does ponytail send data off the machine (suspected RL-3)?
questions.answer: No telemetry in shipped code; the only outbound call is an opt-in, https-only webhook to a user-configured address. The suspicion came from benchmark fixture text. Local data is kept by default and is not removed on uninstall.

questions.question: Is it a skill pack or an agent tool, and is its runtime code safe?
questions.answer: A skill pack: the product is agent behaviour from one prompt. Its hooks and band use argv-array process calls, path allowlists, a regex timeout and output escaping; the gaps are untested band code in CI and missing untrusted-content rules in review and audit.
